# Cwift (cwift.com)

> Cwift provides 24-hour desktop appraisals of California single-family homes and condominiums. Reports are prepared and signed by Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser (license AR036053, California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers), appraising since 2004, 7,000+ appraisals. Delivery is within 24 hours of payment and photos, seven days a week. Cwift is a service of Brian Ward Appraisal (https://www.brianward.com); its sister site date-of-death.com offers the same reports on a standard schedule.

## Key facts
- Service: desktop residential appraisal under USPAP (no site visit; client photos, public records, MLS data, comparable sales analysis)
- 24-hour fees: Basic Desktop $450; Standard Desktop $675
- Standard turnaround: Basic $299, Standard $449, delivered in 5–10 business days
- The 24-hour clock: The 24-hour clock starts when both your payment and your photos and property details have arrived, and it runs seven days a week, weekends and holidays included.
- Coverage: all 58 California counties
- Properties: single-family homes and condominiums, including townhomes and PUD homes; not 2–4 unit buildings, apartment buildings, commercial property and vacant land; not for mortgage lending
- Contact: email contact@cwift.com or the online order form at https://www.cwift.com/order (no phone line; email and online submission are the fastest way to receive service)
- Photos: upload at https://www.cwift.com/upload or attach to email
- Suitability: Brian Ward has prepared desktop appraisals for every purpose listed on this site. Some situations still call for an inspection-based appraisal, so check with your attorney or tax advisor before you order to be sure a desktop report fits your matter.

## Purposes (date of death listed first)
- [Date of Death & Step-Up in Basis](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/date-of-death): Retrospective value on the date of death to support the heirs' new tax basis.
- [Trust & Estate Administration](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/trust-estate): Certified values for trustees and executors: accountings, distributions and trust sales.
- [Divorce & Family Law](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/divorce): Current or date-of-separation values for buyouts, mediation and settlement talks.
- [Family Transfers & Co-Owner Buyouts](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/family-transfers): A fair, documented price when a home changes hands inside the family.
- [Gift Tax (Form 709)](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/gift-tax): Fair market value of gifted real estate on the date of transfer, for the gift-tax return.
- [Prop 19 Parent-Child Transfers](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/prop-19): Market value on the transfer date, to see how much of the old tax base survives.
- [Property Tax Appeals](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/property-tax-appeal): Independent market value evidence for Prop 8 reviews and assessment appeals.
- [Bankruptcy](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/bankruptcy): Home values for Chapter 7 and 13 schedules, exemptions and plan math.
- [Pre-Listing Pricing](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/pre-listing): An independent value before you set the list price.
- [Pre-Purchase Value Check](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/pre-purchase): An independent price check while your contingency period is still open.
- [Immigration Sponsors (Form I-864)](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/immigration): Home equity documented for an I-864 Affidavit of Support.
- [Bail & Property Bonds](https://www.cwift.com/purposes/bail-bonds): Current value to document equity for a property bond or bail collateral.

## FAQ

### The 24-hour service
Q: When does the 24-hour clock start?
A: When both your payment and your photos and property details have arrived. From that moment the appraisal is emailed to you within 24 hours, and the clock runs seven days a week, weekends and holidays included.

Q: What happens if I finish my order on a Saturday night?
A: Nothing changes. Weekends and holidays count, so if payment and photos are in at 9 p.m. Saturday, the report is in your inbox by 9 p.m. Sunday.

Q: Is 24-hour delivery available for every property?
A: For most California single-family homes and condominiums, yes. Very old valuation dates, highly unusual properties and orders covering several properties can need more time. Every request is reviewed before invoicing, so you'll know before you pay.

Q: Why does the 24-hour service cost more?
A: It pays for putting your file at the front of the line and finishing it within 24 hours, seven days a week, weekends and holidays included. The research, the analysis and the report itself are the same as on the standard schedule.

Q: What if I don't actually need it within 24 hours?
A: Order the same report at the standard fee ($299 or $449) with delivery in 5–10 business days. The analysis is identical; only the timing changes.

### Desktop appraisals
Q: What is a desktop appraisal?
A: A complete appraisal prepared without a site visit by the appraiser. The appraiser researches the market, selects and adjusts comparable sales, and reconciles a value exactly as in any appraisal, describing the home from your photos, public records, listing history and the details you supply.

Q: Is a desktop appraisal the same as a Zestimate or a broker price opinion?
A: No. Automated estimates are computer models with no appraiser and no accountability, and broker opinions come from licensees who aren't appraisers. A desktop appraisal is developed and signed by a state-certified appraiser under USPAP, with a certification, a workfile and a license that can be checked.

Q: Are desktop appraisals USPAP-compliant?
A: Yes. USPAP leaves the extent of any inspection to the appraiser's scope of work and requires the report to state whether the appraiser personally inspected the property. Cwift reports state plainly that they are desktop appraisals and describe the information relied on.

Q: When is a desktop appraisal the wrong choice?
A: Mortgage lending, cases headed to trial where the other side will challenge every assumption, disputes among beneficiaries, courts or agencies that require an interior inspection, and properties whose condition or features photos can't capture. For those, Brian Ward Appraisal offers inspection-based appraisals.

Q: Have you done desktop appraisals for my purpose before?
A: Brian Ward has prepared desktop appraisals for every purpose listed on this site. Some situations still call for an inspection-based appraisal, so check with your attorney or tax advisor before you order to be sure a desktop report fits your matter.

### Ordering, photos and delivery
Q: Why is there no phone number?
A: Because email and the online form are faster. A written request arrives with the address, the dates and the purpose already spelled out, photos travel in the same message, and nothing waits on a callback. Send questions to contact@cwift.com at any hour.

Q: What photos do you need?
A: The front and back of the house, the kitchen, each bathroom, the main living areas and bedrooms, plus anything that adds or subtracts value: upgrades, a pool, a view, damage, unfinished work. Smartphone photos are fine. For a past date, send photos that show the home as it was then.

Q: Can I send photos before I pay?
A: Yes, and it saves time. Upload them right after you submit your order, or reply to the confirmation email with them. The clock starts the moment payment arrives.

Q: How is the appraisal delivered?
A: As a PDF emailed to you, ready to forward to your CPA, attorney, trustee or the agency that asked for it.

Q: What if the report gets something wrong about my property?
A: If a feature, the condition or the quality of the home was misread or misdescribed, the appraisal is revised at no charge. Tell us what's different and include anything that shows it.

Q: What kinds of property do you appraise?
A: California single-family homes and condominiums, including townhomes and PUD homes. Cwift does not appraise 2–4 unit buildings, apartment buildings, commercial property and vacant land. Luxury homes, large acreage and highly unique properties may need a custom quote.

Q: Do you cover my county?
A: Yes. Desktop appraisals are available for property in all 58 California counties.

Q: Can I use the appraisal to get a mortgage or refinance?
A: No. Lenders must order their own appraisals, and an appraisal can't be readdressed to a new client later. Cwift reports are for tax, legal, estate and personal decisions.

Q: Who actually prepares the appraisal?
A: Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, license AR036053, who has appraised California homes since 2004. No trainees, no outsourcing.

Q: How do I pay?
A: Through the secure online invoice emailed to you after your request is reviewed. Payment and photos start the 24-hour clock.


## Purpose details

### Date of Death & Step-Up in Basis
When a California homeowner dies, the heirs' tax basis in the house generally resets to what the home was worth on the day of death. That number decides how much capital gain an heir reports when the property sells, and escrow, a tax preparer's calendar or an eager buyer can leave very little time to produce it. Cwift prepares the retrospective appraisal that documents the value and emails it within 24 hours once payment and photos are in.
Many families learn they need a basis appraisal late in the process: the house is already in escrow, the CPA is finishing the final returns, or a trustee is about to distribute proceeds. A 24-hour report keeps the sale and the filing moving without falling back on an online estimate that won't hold up.
- The home's market value on the day of death, or on the alternate valuation date six months later when the executor elects it under IRC §2032.
- Comparable sales that closed around the valuation date rather than today's market.
- The home's condition as it was then, reconstructed from your photos and records when it has changed since.
- Support for California's community property rule, under which both halves of community property can receive a new basis when one spouse dies (IRC §1014(b)(6)).
Desktop suitability: Date-of-death work is where desktop appraisals make the most sense. Nobody can walk through the house as it stood on a past date; the analysis rests on sales from that period and on evidence of the home's condition at the time. A site visit today would document today's house, which may not be the house that matters. If beneficiaries are likely to argue about the value, an inspection-based appraisal can carry more weight. Ask your attorney before ordering.
Q: Can you appraise a date of death from many years ago?
A: Yes. Retrospective appraisals are routine, and Brian has completed them for dates several decades back. Very old dates can require extra research, so 24-hour delivery is confirmed before you pay.
Q: Will the IRS accept the report?
A: The IRS doesn't pre-approve appraisers or report formats. It looks for a credible, well-supported valuation by a qualified appraiser. Cwift reports are prepared under USPAP and signed by a California Certified Residential appraiser, and your tax advisor can confirm what your return needs.
Q: The house was remodeled after the death. Is that a problem?
A: No. Send whatever shows the earlier condition: old listing photos, family pictures, permits or contractor invoices. The value is developed as of the date of death, not as the house looks now.

### Trust & Estate Administration
A trustee or executor is expected to know what the trust or estate holds, what it is worth, and how that number was reached. A desktop appraisal gives you a signed, certified value you can put in an accounting, use to balance distributions, or show a beneficiary who asks where the figure came from.
A beneficiary meeting is set for Monday. A buyer wants to close. The CPA needs values to finish the fiduciary return. When the real estate value is the last open item, 24-hour delivery takes it off the list.
- Valuing the residence on the date of death for the trust's records and the beneficiaries' basis.
- Current value for a distribution in kind, or for a sale of the home to one of the beneficiaries.
- Balancing shares when one heir keeps the house and the others receive cash.
- Supporting the real estate figures in a trustee's accounting.
- Setting the asking price before the trust lists the property.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals suit most administration tasks, particularly when a fiduciary needs a defensible number quickly and the property's condition is well documented. In a formal California probate, real estate on the inventory is appraised by the court's probate referee; a private appraisal can still support pricing, distributions and the heirs' tax basis. If co-trustees or beneficiaries are already at odds over value, consider an inspection-based appraisal, and ask your attorney how a private appraisal fits your case.
Q: Can I get the date-of-death value and today's value at the same time?
A: Yes. Both opinions of value can be developed in one assignment if you ask for them when you order. The fee and the delivery time are confirmed on your invoice before you pay.
Q: Who is allowed to rely on the appraisal?
A: The client named in the report and the intended users listed in it, typically the trustee, the attorney and the CPA. Name everyone who needs to rely on it when you place the order.

### Divorce & Family Law
In a California divorce the family home is often the largest community asset, and settlement talks stall until someone puts a credible number on the table. Cwift prepares independent desktop appraisals for spouses, attorneys and mediators, whether you need a current value, a date-of-separation value or both.
Mediation sessions, settlement conferences and disclosure deadlines usually get calendared before anyone thinks to order an appraisal. A report that arrives within 24 hours lets you negotiate from evidence instead of a guess.
- Calculating a buyout when one spouse keeps the house.
- Equalizing a property division with other assets or payments.
- Deciding whether to sell the home or keep it.
- Supporting a settlement proposal or a mediator's recommendation.
- Values on more than one date, since California Family Code §2552 generally values community assets near the time of trial but lets the court choose another date for good cause.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals work well for negotiation, mediation and agreed buyouts, where both sides mainly need an independent figure built from real sales. If the case is headed to trial and the other side may challenge every assumption, an inspection-based appraisal with expert testimony can be the stronger tool. Brian provides those through Brian Ward Appraisal.
Q: My spouse lives in the house and won't let anyone in. Can you still appraise it?
A: Usually, yes. Public records, prior listing photos and your own knowledge of the home are often enough for a credible desktop appraisal, and the report states what it relied on.
Q: Can the appraisal be used in court?
A: Reports are prepared under USPAP and signed by a certified appraiser, and Brian has testified as an expert witness in family law matters. Whether a desktop report is the right exhibit for your hearing is a question for your attorney.

### Family Transfers & Co-Owner Buyouts
Selling the family home to one of the kids, buying a sibling out of an inherited house, or untangling a co-ownership between friends or partners: each of these deals goes more smoothly when everyone starts from the same independent value.
Agreements tend to form over a holiday weekend, before a relative flies home, or the day an attorney is ready to draft the paperwork. With 24-hour delivery the number arrives while everyone is still at the table.
- It gives co-owners a buyout figure nobody chose to suit themselves.
- It documents an arm's-length price if a sale below market value is later treated as part gift.
- It records the new owner's value for future tax and insurance questions.
- It turns a conversation about feelings into a conversation about sales.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals suit family transactions well: the people who know the house best supply the information, and everyone can see exactly what the appraisal relied on. 
Q: If I sell to my child below market value, do I need an appraisal?
A: The gap between fair market value and the price paid can count as a gift for federal gift-tax purposes, so many families document the value. Your tax advisor can tell you whether a gift-tax return is required.
Q: Can I use the appraisal to get a mortgage for the buyout?
A: No. Lenders order their own appraisals. A Cwift report is for pricing and documenting the transfer, not for loan underwriting.

### Gift Tax (Form 709)
Transferring a house, or part of one, to a relative or into a trust? The gift's fair market value on the date of transfer belongs on the federal gift-tax return, and an appraisal from a qualified appraiser is the usual way to support it.
Form 709 is generally due by April 15 of the year after the gift, and planning moves such as deeding a share into a trust or closing a family sale before December 31 tend to pile up near deadlines. A 24-hour report keeps the return from waiting on the appraisal.
- Treasury regulations describe what an appraisal attached to a gift-tax return should contain: the dates, a description of the property, the appraisal process, assumptions and limiting conditions, the information considered, the methods, and the reasoning behind the value (Treas. Reg. §301.6501(c)-1(f)(3)).
- Adequate disclosure starts the IRS's three-year window to question the reported value; without it, that window can stay open.
- The regulation's appraiser requirements cover qualifications and independence, so the appraiser can't be the donor, the recipient or a family member.
Desktop suitability: The adequate-disclosure rules focus on the appraiser's qualifications and the contents of the report. They don't call for a physical inspection, and for most single-family and condominium gifts a desktop appraisal supplies what the return needs. Cwift values the property itself; if you are giving a fractional interest, any discount for a partial interest is a separate analysis, typically by a business valuation specialist. 
Q: Do I need an appraisal if the gift is small?
A: Most real estate gifts exceed the annual exclusion, but thresholds change. Your CPA or attorney can confirm whether a return is required and how the value should be supported.
Q: Can you appraise a gift that was made last year?
A: Yes. The appraisal is developed as of the transfer date, using sales from that period.

### Prop 19 Parent-Child Transfers
Since February 16, 2021, Proposition 19 has narrowed California's parent-child property tax exclusion. A family home keeps part of its low assessment only when a child, or a qualifying grandchild, makes it their principal residence, and only up to a value cap. The home's market value on the transfer date tells you how much of the old assessment survives.
Move in, rent it out, sell it, or buy out siblings: each choice changes the tax bill, and families often have to decide quickly. The assessor's claim forms carry their own deadlines too.
- For transfers from February 16, 2025 through February 15, 2027, the exclusion covers the parent's factored base year value plus $1,044,586. Market value above that limit is added to the assessment (State Board of Equalization).
- Earlier windows used $1,000,000 (Feb 16, 2021 to Feb 15, 2023) and $1,022,600 (through Feb 15, 2025); the amount adjusts every two years.
- Parent-to-child transfers are claimed on form BOE-19-P with the county assessor; grandparent-to-grandchild transfers use BOE-19-G.
Desktop suitability: County assessors set values from sales data and records, generally without walking through the house. A desktop appraisal works from the same kind of evidence, examined property by property, which makes it a natural fit for Prop 19 planning and for questioning an assessor's figure. 
Q: Does the appraisal set my new property tax?
A: No. The county assessor sets the assessed value. The appraisal gives you an independent market value to plan with and, if needed, evidence for a review or appeal of the assessor's figure.
Q: What if the assessor's market value seems too high?
A: An independent appraisal of market value on the transfer date is the evidence you would bring to an informal review or a formal assessment appeal.

### Property Tax Appeals
When a home's market value falls below its assessed value, Proposition 8 allows a temporary reduction. If the assessor won't agree, the county assessment appeals board hears the evidence, and an independent appraisal is the kind of evidence boards are used to weighing.
Regular appeal applications are filed between July 2 and either September 15 or November 30, depending on the county (State Board of Equalization). Appraisals ordered in the final days of the window are where 24-hour delivery earns its keep.
- Prop 8 decline-in-value requests to the assessor.
- Formal assessment appeals before the county board or a hearing officer.
- Questioning a base-year value set after a purchase, an inheritance or other change in ownership.
Desktop suitability: Appeals boards decide on evidence of market value, and a well-supported desktop appraisal presents the same comparable-sales evidence as an inspected one. If your county or hearing officer prefers a particular report format, ask before you order.
Q: Will an appraisal guarantee a lower assessment?
A: No one can promise that. The appraisal provides independent evidence of market value, which the board weighs against the assessor's evidence.
Q: Which date should the appraisal use?
A: For a decline-in-value appeal, January 1 of the tax year in question, the lien date. Tell us the year and the effective date is set to match.

### Bankruptcy
Bankruptcy schedules ask for the current value of the debtor's real estate, and that number ripples through the whole case: how much equity the homestead exemption protects, what a Chapter 7 trustee might pursue, and what a Chapter 13 plan has to pay unsecured creditors.
A foreclosure sale date, a wage garnishment or a meeting of creditors can compress the timeline. When counsel needs the value before the petition goes out, a 24-hour appraisal fits the schedule.
- Real property values on Schedule A/B.
- Equity and homestead exemption analysis under California's rules.
- Chapter 13 plan feasibility and the liquidation comparison.
- Responding when a trustee or creditor proposes a different value.
Desktop suitability: Desktop appraisals are widely used to set schedule values and plan a case. Photos, contractor bids and descriptions of defects all feed into the condition rating and the comparable adjustments. If the trustee or a creditor contests value, your attorney may want an inspection-based appraisal and expert testimony, which Brian also provides through Brian Ward Appraisal.
Q: Should the value be as of the filing date?
A: Schedules generally use value as of the petition date, and your attorney will specify. A past date is no problem; retrospective appraisals are routine.
Q: Can a desktop appraisal account for needed repairs?
A: Yes. Send photos of the problems along with any bids or estimates, and they are reflected in the analysis.

### Pre-Listing Pricing
An agent's suggested list price is a marketing opinion. An appraisal is an independent opinion of market value from someone with nothing riding on the sale. Trustees, executors and owners selling without an agent use a pre-listing appraisal to anchor the price and to answer the buyer's appraiser later.
The photographer is booked, the agent is ready and the market moves weekly. A 24-hour appraisal lets you settle the price before the listing goes live instead of cutting it after the home sits.
- A list price backed by recent comparable sales.
- A neutral check on competing agents' pricing opinions.
- Trust and estate sales, where the fiduciary should be able to show the price was reasonable.
- Sales data in hand before the buyer's lender appraisal comes back.
Desktop suitability: Pricing doesn't require an inspection; it requires good comparables and an honest read of the market, which is exactly what a desktop appraisal delivers. 
Q: Will the buyer's lender accept my appraisal?
A: No. The buyer's lender orders its own appraisal. Yours helps you set a supportable price and gives you sales data to discuss if that appraisal comes in low.
Q: Can you value the home as if planned repairs were done?
A: Often, yes. Describe the repairs when you order and you'll get an answer before you're invoiced.

### Pre-Purchase Value Check
Buyers paying cash, buying from family, or competing without an appraisal contingency still want to know whether the price makes sense. A pre-purchase desktop appraisal gives you an independent opinion of market value while you can still negotiate or walk away.
California purchase contracts give buyers a limited window to investigate and remove contingencies. A report delivered within 24 hours fits inside that window with room to act on it.
- Cash buyers who won't have a lender's appraisal.
- Buyers who waived the appraisal contingency to win the offer.
- Off-market and family purchases with no listing history to lean on.
- Anyone who wants a second opinion on a price they've been quoted.
Desktop suitability: Buyers rarely spend more than a showing inside a house before the contingency clock runs out. A desktop appraisal works from listing photos, disclosures and your observations, plus the same market analysis any appraisal uses. 
Q: Can I use this appraisal for my mortgage?
A: No. Your lender must order its own appraisal under appraiser-independence rules. This report is for your own decision.
Q: What about a duplex or vacant land?
A: Cwift appraises single-family homes and condominiums only. For other property types, contact Brian Ward Appraisal.

### Immigration Sponsors (Form I-864)
A sponsor whose income falls short of the I-864 requirement can count assets, and the equity in a home can be one of them. The I-864 instructions define a home's net value as its appraised value minus every loan secured by it, and they ask sponsors who use it to include a recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser.
Requests for evidence from the National Visa Center or USCIS carry response dates, and one missing document can hold up an entire case. A 24-hour appraisal clears that item quickly.
- Proof of ownership, such as the deed.
- A recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser establishing the home's value.
- Statements for every mortgage or lien, so net equity can be calculated.
- Assets count only if they can be converted to cash within one year without considerable hardship, and officers decide how much weight real estate deserves.
Desktop suitability: The I-864 instructions ask for a recent appraisal by a licensed appraiser; they don't specify an inspection. A desktop appraisal from a California Certified Residential appraiser documents value quickly and clearly. Your immigration attorney can advise whether relying on home equity makes sense in your case.
Q: How recent does the appraisal need to be?
A: The instructions ask for a recent appraisal, so order close to the date you'll submit the evidence.
Q: Can I use the home I live in?
A: The I-864 instructions allow sponsors to include the net value of their home as an asset, subject to the rules on assets. Your attorney can confirm how they apply to you.

### Bail & Property Bonds
California lets a property owner post real estate equity instead of cash bail under Penal Code §1298, but the court must find that the equity is at least twice the bail amount. That finding starts with a current appraisal.
When the appraisal is the last document missing from the property-bond packet, 24-hour delivery gets the packet to the clerk sooner.
- Superior courts publish their own property-bond instructions, and many call for an appraisal by a California-licensed or certified appraiser with the license number on the report.
- Some courts require the appraisal to be recent, for example within the last six months, and some specify a report form.
- Bail agents who accept real estate as collateral often want an appraisal to confirm the equity.
Desktop suitability: Many courts accept an appraisal without specifying an inspection, but requirements vary by county. Check your court's packet or ask your bail agent before ordering. If an inspected appraisal is required, Brian Ward Appraisal provides them in San Diego and Riverside Counties.
Q: Does the equity need to be twice the bail?
A: Under Penal Code §1298 the court must find that the equity is at least twice the bail amount. Equity is the appraised value minus the loans and liens against the property.
Q: Do bail agents accept property as collateral?
A: Many do. Ask the agent which report and effective date they need before you order.


## Credibility brief

### The standards don't require a site visit
USPAP, published by the Appraisal Standards Board of The Appraisal Foundation, is the set of standards appraisers follow throughout the United States, and California law requires licensed appraisers to comply with it. The current edition took effect on January 1, 2024, and has no end date.
Its Scope of Work Rule makes the appraiser responsible for deciding what research and analysis are needed to produce credible results for the intended use. Advisory Opinion 2 treats the extent of any inspection as part of that scope of work, which can vary with the assignment. What USPAP does require is disclosure: the certification must state whether the appraiser personally inspected the property, and the report must describe the information relied on.

### Lenders already rely on desktop appraisals
Fannie Mae's Selling Guide (B4-1.2-02) describes desktop appraisals reported on Form 1004 Desktop, whose minimum scope of work does not require a current inspection of the property or the comparable sales. The appraiser relies on data from other sources. They are eligible for certain one-unit, principal-residence purchase loans with loan-to-value ratios of 90% or less.
Freddie Mac accepts desktop appraisals for eligible purchase transactions as well. If the companies that back home mortgages accept desktop appraisals for loans secured by the house, the method is credible for the estate, tax and family decisions on this site.

### Tax rules focus on who signs and what the report says
For gift-tax returns, Treasury regulations describe an appraisal that satisfies adequate disclosure (26 CFR §301.6501(c)-1(f)(3)). The appraiser must regularly perform appraisals, be qualified for the type of property, and be independent of the donor and the recipient. The report must state the dates and purpose, describe the property and the appraisal process, list assumptions and limiting conditions, identify the information considered, and explain the procedures, the method and the specific basis for the value. None of those requirements is a physical inspection.
For inherited property, the heir's basis is generally the fair market value at the date of death (IRC §1014). The appraisal is the documentation of that value, and its credibility rests on the appraiser's qualifications and the quality of the analysis.

### Comparable sales have always been studied remotely
In any appraisal, inspected or not, the appraiser does not tour the comparable sales. Their features and condition come from MLS records, listing photographs, public records and market data. Most of the evidence behind any value opinion is gathered this way. A desktop appraisal applies the same research method to the subject property.

### The owner's evidence is often better than a short visit
Photographs of every room, measurements, permits, invoices and the owner's account of repairs can document a home more completely than a brief walk-through, especially for the work nobody can see. When information turns out to be wrong, the remedy is built in: Cwift revises the appraisal at no charge if the home's features, quality or condition were misread or misdescribed.

### Past dates can't be inspected anyway
Date-of-death, gift, separation and transfer appraisals value a home as it was on an earlier date. A visit today would document today's condition, after a clean-out, repairs or a remodel. The credible approach, in any format, is to reconstruct the earlier condition from evidence and to rely on sales from that period.

### The appraiser is fully accountable
Every Cwift report is signed by Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, license AR036053, issued by the California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers (BREA), which licenses and disciplines appraisers. The license can be verified with BREA's public appraiser search. USPAP requires the appraiser to keep a workfile supporting each report for at least five years, and longer when testimony is involved, so the analysis can be examined if the value is ever questioned.

Sources:
- The Appraisal Foundation, Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP), 2024 edition: https://www.appraisalfoundation.org/imis/TAF/Standards/Appraisal_Standards/Uniform_Standards_of_Professional_Appraisal_Practice/TAF/USPAP.aspx
